en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty Fifth Chapter
The Discussion on Conventional Knowledge:
Should it not be said that conventional knowledge has only the truths as its object and nothing else as its object?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Is it not the case that for one who has attained the meditative absorption on the earth-kasiṇa, there is knowledge, and that the earth-kasiṇa is conventional truth?
“Yes.”
If there is knowledge for one who has attained the earth-kasiṇa absorption, and the earth-kasiṇa is a conventional truth (sammutisacca), then indeed it should be said:
"Conventional knowledge has only conventional truth as its object, not anything else.
It should not be so said.
“Is conventional knowledge (sammutiñāṇa) directed only toward the truths as its object, and not toward anything else?”—
“Yes. … [as before] … But is it not the case that the water-kasiṇa … [and so on]?
Is there knowledge for one giving the fire-kasiṇa …pe… medicinal requisites as support for the sick, and are the medicinal requisites as support for the sick conventional truth?
Yes.
If, for one giving medicinal requisites as support for the sick, there is knowledge, and the medicinal requisites as support for the sick are conventional truth, then indeed, sir, you must say:
“Conventional knowledge has only conventional truth as its object, not anything else.
Is it the case that conventional knowledge has only conventional truth as its object and nothing else?
“Yes,” you say.
“Does one, by means of that knowledge, fully understand suffering, abandon its origin, realize its cessation, and develop the path?
One should not speak thus … [and so on].
The Discussion on Conventional Knowledge is finished.
